Subject: Initial: SCCs — module question and evidence request

Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking this. Crestline Legal is preparing our contract packet for the upcoming engagement and needs confirmation on the transfer mechanism for EU/UK personal data. Specifically:

1) Which SCC module will Redwood Inference sign for Crestline (we are a Controller; you are a Processor)?
2) If you expect to rely on a different module or combination (e.g., UK Addendum + specific EU modules), please confirm and provide the operative text you propose.
3) Operational evidence for Processor safeguards we typically assess: the DPA, DPIA summary, SOC 2 status (or link to the report), and any technical/organizational supplementary measures you recommend.

I've attached a short questionnaire (Crestline_SCCs_Request.pdf) with the items we need. Our timeline is tight — legal needs the signed SCCs + DPA countersigned or a DocuSign package by end of next week.

Happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

Thanks,
Sarah Bennet
Senior Counsel, Crestline Therapeutics

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Initial: SCCs — module question and evidence request

Hi Sarah / Peter — thanks for the clear list. Apologies for the quick turnaround but below is our proposed approach and the materials you requested.

Proposed transfer mechanism
- Redwood's role for this engagement: Processor (we process personal data on behalf of Crestline).
- Recommended SCC module: Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) as published in the EU Commission SCC set applicable to controller-to-processor transfers.
- For transfers to the UK, we will execute the UK Addendum alongside the EU clauses (this is our standard approach where UK data is in scope).
- If Crestline prefers a combined EU module + UK-specific text baked into a single DocuSign envelope, we can provide that as well.

Operative text / execution options
- Option A (preferred): Crestline signs the EU Controller-to-Processor SCCs (Module 2) and Redwood signs (DocuSign). UK Addendum executed as a separate addendum page where UK personal data is indicated.
- Option B: Crestline executes an EU+UK consolidated package (we will generate a single envelope with both clause sets).

Operational evidence (attached)
- DPA_v3.1_Redwood.pdf — our current Data Processing Agreement with standard exhibits.
- DPIA_Summary_Crestline.xlsx — short summary addressing data flows and relevant mitigations for the planned processing.
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II; we can provide an access link for reviewers and a redacted report under NDA. Please advise if you'd like the full report; we'll route via our GRC portal.
- Technical controls to note: AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS1.3 in transit, role-based access controls, centralized key management (KMS), KV cache TTL controls to limit retention.

DocuSign and timing
- I've prepared a draft DocuSign package (DocuSign link below) that includes Module 2 plus the UK Addendum as an attached addendum. If this is acceptable we can send the envelope for signature today; counter-signature target within 3 business days.

Links / attachments
- DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/exec/12345
- DPA (attached): DPA_v3.1_Redwood.pdf
- DPIA executive summary (attached): DPIA_Summary_Crestline.xlsx

Please let me know if you prefer a different module approach (we can discuss processor-to-processor flows if Crestline will direct onward transfers to sub-processors), or if legal wants the redlined clause text.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Principal Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com

Attachments: DPA_v3.1_Redwood.pdf (PDF, 95KB); DPIA_Summary_Crestline.xlsx (XLSX, 12KB)

Marissa — this is exactly what we needed. Module 2 + UK Addendum works for Crestline. A couple of items before we proceed to signature:

1) Can you confirm whether any of the subprocessors operate outside the EU/UK (we'll need to list locations in our packet)?
2) Please send the DocuSign envelope for signature and include the DPA v3.1 as a supporting document in the envelope.
3) We'll request SOC 2 access under NDA — send the contact or process to request it and we'll route internally.

Once we have that we should be able to circulate for internal approval and sign within your proposed timeline.

Thanks,
Sarah
